forecasts.reason: About 12 more frozen steps at roughly 10 ms each saves about 0.11 s. Starting the anneal at the 70% switch takes away group 2's 32 px adaptation at full LR, which I expect to cost 0.05–0.2 pp. That is within rebuild noise, so the run won't settle whether there is a cliff.

About 35 skipped stem backwards at around 6 ms each saves about 0.2 s. I think the freezes are neutral because the anneal acts as a per-layer cooldown, not because the stem gets sparse updates. An un-annealed half-rate stem near peak LR drops the cooldown benefit, so I expect a small loss of about 0.1 pp.

About 9 more truncated steps saves only about 0.07 s. A steeper group-1 anneal plus almost no 32 px stem training should cost about 0.1 pp. The 0.07 s saving is about one noise SD, so this cannot separate a cliff from a linear dose.

Inductor already fuses the GELU backward and recomputes it from the saved pre-activation, so ReLU saves only part of the read bytes. I project a 1.5–2.5% saving, likely below the 3% gate. If the swap does run, CIFAR-100 should lose 0.2–0.4 pp from dropping GELU.

The time depends on which cuts pass, and the top-up adds about 0.13 s. The cuts' losses each sit near their gates, so after stacking, the margin from the top-up roughly cancels. I expect about 1–3% faster at near-equal accuracy, with the result decided by noise.

cruxes: Are annealed freezes neutral because the per-layer LR anneal acts as a beneficial early cooldown, rather than because the frozen block has finished learning? If so, un-annealed sparse updates (I084) lose more than the dose predicts, and freezes with a longer anneal could even gain accuracy.

Is the rebuild spread (SD about 0.2 pp on the 3-seed mean) removable by pinning kernels? If not, every remaining 0.05–0.15 pp lever is untestable against the 0.753 gate, and only cuts of ≥2% time that are near-free (lazy last-epoch augmentation, skipping Lookahead over frozen params) are worth running.
Does group 2 have a cliff at the 70% resolution switch, as group 1 did in E037? This decides whether the freeze cascade has any dose left or is used up at 90%.
structured_output.world_model: W5, after E051. The tip is E049 (5.198 s, population mean about 0.754, rebuild SD about 0.2 pp). Mechanism nobody has proposed yet: the annealed freezes are not just 'free' truncations. The per-group LR anneal to 0 works as a layerwise early cooldown that partly offsets the lost updates, which is why E028 and E046 were neutral and the abrupt or early freezes (E037) were not. So intermittent backward without an anneal (I084) should do worse than its saved-gradient fraction implies, and moving freeze points earlier mostly shortens the cooldown at full resolution. Remaining dose levers (I083, I085) each save about 0.07–0.12 s for about 0.1 pp, roughly the dial rate (about 1–1.5 s/pp), so they are not dominant. ReLU probably saves under 3% because Inductor already fuses the GELU backward. Untried identical-math cuts are lazy last-epoch augmentation and skipping Lookahead lerp/copy for frozen params, worth about 1–2%. Every result now sits inside noise unless kernel selection is pinned.
